statement: Recombinant rat GluN1-1a/GluN2A in oocytes (22-24 C, Mg-free Ba-Ringer, 200 uM NMDA + 10 uM glycine, -70 mV) has a proton midpoint pIC50 7.21 and Hill slope 1.45, current normalised to pH 9.
The same receptor with the GluN1 exon-5 insert (NR1-1b/NR2A) has pIC50 6.96 and a steeper Hill slope 2.70: exon 5 lowers proton sensitivity by 0.25 pH units in this system.

From the fitted pIC50 and slope (zero floor assumed, pH 9 reference) the fraction of GluN1-1a/2A current at pH 7.4, 7.2, 7.0 is about 0.65, 0.49, 0.33; for exon-5 form about 0.94, 0.82, 0.56. Between 7.4 and 7.2 that is a 25 percent and a 13 percent loss. No residual current is stated by the source.

In the review compilation of rat recombinant data GluN1/GluN2B has a proton midpoint at pH 7.3-7.5 and GluN1/GluN2A at pH 6.74-7.20; in the same-study neighbours (Yi 2018) GluN1-1a/2B is pH 7.54 and GluN1-1a/2A pH 6.80. The prior ordering (2A more sensitive than 2B) is not what the compilation shows. Conditions per entry are not carried by the review. [V7: GluN2B vs GluN2A: 'GluN2B less proton-sensitive than GluN2A' is CONTRADICTED for recombinant diheteromers (Hansen 2021 Table 5; Tian 2021; Regan 2019). Honest fractions (7.4/7.2/7.0): GluN2A 0.61-0.85 / 0.47-0.74 / 0.31-0.65; GluN2B 0.35-0.56 / 0.22-0.44 / 0.13-0.33. Loss for 7.4 to 7.2: GluN2A 9-26 percent, GluN2B 21-36 percent. Ends of the ranges use Hill 1 (assumed).]

No proton midpoint, slope or residual for a GluN1/GluN2A/GluN2B triheteromer was found in the compiled table (H+ column empty for GluN1/2A/2B), the founding triheteromer paper, or the triheteromer pharmacology paper. Perimeter: three sources and the strings in queries.tsv; unknown is not negative.

Indirect triheteromer facts: at pH 6.4 spermine inhibits the triheteromer current (GluN1/2A-like) while at 7.3 it potentiates (GluN1/2B-like) in HEK cells; and Zn2+ maximal inhibition at pH 6.8 is 65 percent for the triheteromer vs 93 percent for GluN1/2A, so a single GluN2A site gives less Zn-enhanced proton inhibition.

Native NMDA current of acutely isolated juvenile (P13-P19) rat prefrontal-cortex pyramidal neurons is inhibited by protons with pH50 6.97 (IC50 0.11 uM, steady-state NMDA, reference pH 7.6) at 22-24 C without Mg2+.

In the same neurons a step from 7.6 to 7.1 with protons applied first inhibited NMDA current by 22 +/- 7 percent (peak) and 26 +/- 3 percent (steady state), n=5; applied together with NMDA the peak was unchanged and the steady state fell by 28 +/- 5 percent. Reading the 7.4 point off the raster (about 0.88) puts the 7.4-to-7.1 change at about 11 percent (INFERENZA).

No experiment in the sources read separates the proton effect on native NMDA current by subunit (no GluN2B-selective tool in a pH series). Perimeter: this package plus queries Q05-Q08 and Q13; unknown is not negative.

Recombinant human ASIC1a (CHO, 20-25 C) activates with pH50 about 6.5; the steady-state activation data give about 2-3 percent of maximum at pH 7.0 and about 5 percent at 6.8; no activation is resolvable at 7.2-7.4. The model of the same paper needs a drop to pH 6.7 or lower to produce current or charge.

Steady-state desensitisation (60 s conditioning, I2/I1): about 1.0 at pH 7.4, about 0.84 at 7.2, about 0.46 at 7.1, about 0.06 at 7.0; midpoint about 7.1 from the data, while the fitted model function has pH50 7.26 (computed). A fall from 7.4 to 7.2 therefore desensitises about 16 percent of channels in 60 s and opens none. [V7: see PS17 note; the model charge transport at pH 7.0-7.15 'was not observed in experiments' (Alijevic), omitted by the producer.]
Native: in juvenile rat cortical pyramidal neurons no significant ASIC current is seen at pH 7.1 (pH50 6.19); in embryonic mouse cortical neuron culture pH50 is 6.29 +/- 0.23 (ASIC2-/- 6.67).

No source reached puts K2P, NMDAR and ASIC on one juvenile layer II/III neuron in a pH step. Two-target co-measurement exists: NMDAR plus ASIC on the same cortical pyramidal neuron (P13-P19, room temperature, Mg-free, pH 7.6 reference), where the total glutamate response fell 20 +/- 7 percent at 6.8 and 19 +/- 8 percent (NMDA, total) at 6.5 because ASIC compensates. No K2P measure in it.

A fourth proton target acts on the same cell class: acid shifts in pHo reduce CA1 pyramidal firing (not interneuron firing) independently of ASIC1a, attributed in part to NaV1.2 (abstract only; pH step size and numbers unread).

All proton-sensitivity values found for NMDAR and ASIC1a are from 20-25 C preparations; no 30-37 C source for either was found (perimeter: sources read plus strings Q05-Q13). Mg2+ appears only as a single 1 mM test without a pH series. The net-sign rule therefore lacks a common-axis NMDAR magnitude at physiological Mg2+ and temperature and must state directions only. [V7: overclaim: 'all values 20-25 C' should read 'all values with a stated temperature'; the compiled Hansen rows and Evlanenkov state none.]
